candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions and infection prevention
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — VRE/MDRO precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply setting-specific CDC precautions for known VRE colonization in an acute-care hospital.

options.A: Use Standard Precautions plus Contact Precautions for the known target-MDRO colonization according to the hospital's infection-control program
options.B: Use Airborne Precautions because VRE is primarily transmitted through airborne droplet nuclei
options.C: Use no precautions because colonization cannot contribute to healthcare transmission
options.D: Use Droplet Precautions alone and omit Standard Precautions

candidate.rationale: CDC MDRO guidance for acute-care hospitals recommends routine Contact Precautions for patients infected with target MDROs and for patients previously identified as colonized, while Standard Precautions remain foundational. VRE is transmitted mainly through direct or indirect contact, including contaminated environmental surfaces and equipment, not through the airborne route.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In acute-care hospitals, known colonization with a target MDRO such as VRE calls for Contact Precautions in addition to Standard Precautions under CDC guidance.
candidate.source_document_title: Management of Multidrug-Resistant Organisms in Healthcare Settings — Summary of Recommendations
candidate.source_locator: V.A.5.c.i Acute-care hospitals — implement Contact Precautions routinely for patients infected with target MDROs and known colonized patients; Standard Precautions remain required
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.source_version_date: CDC web update March–April 2024; current guidance accessed 2026
candidate.stem: An adult admitted to an acute-care hospital is known to be colonized with vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE). Which transmission-based approach is most appropriate under CDC MDRO guidance?
